title: Deepika Padukone's Baby Bump Just Upstaged a ₹119 Crore Bandra Penthouse
excerpt: Bollywood's first couple was spotted at their sea-facing quadruplex — and Deepika, glowing with baby number two, looked like she was already the most expensive thing on that balcony.
body:
The photos weren't supposed to happen. **Deepika Padukone** and **Ranveer Singh** had kept things deliberately quiet since the pregnancy announcement in April — no pap walks, no coordinated airport looks, no carefully leaked pictures outside a dubbing studio. Then on Sunday evening, someone with a long lens and zero boundaries caught them on the balcony of their new Bandra home, and the internet promptly lost its collective mind.

The images are simple and devastating. Deepika in a loose white co-ord set, her baby bump unmistakable in the golden-hour light. Ranveer in a red vest and black track pants, animated and gesturing, probably arguing about where to put a sofa. Behind them: the Arabian Sea, stretching out like a private backdrop they paid ₹119 crore for. Because they did.

> "That's my parents 🥹🥰" — Fan account @jviciouslady on X, June 8, 2026

The Bandra Bandstand property — a sea-facing quadruplex reportedly purchased in 2022 — has been one of Mumbai real estate's worst-kept secrets. The couple had visited for a final inspection of the interior work, sources say, ahead of a planned move-in after the baby arrives. From the terrace, they looked out at a city that has spent the better part of a decade being obsessed with them.

## The Announcement That Broke April

Deepika and Ranveer confirmed baby number two on April 19 with the kind of Instagram post that makes you feel things. Their daughter **Dua**, born September 8, 2024, was pictured holding a positive pregnancy test — two red lines, no caption needed beyond a pair of 🧿 emojis. The internet did the rest.

This was one of Deepika's first public appearances since that post. She's been filming through the early months — wrapping her portions for **King** alongside **Shah Rukh Khan** (the reunion the diaspora has been screaming for since *Chennai Express*) and reportedly completing work on **Raaka**, the **Atlee**-directed sci-fi spectacle opposite **Allu Arjun**. Both films are expected to arrive later this year, which means Deepika has been quietly stacking two of the biggest releases of 2026 while growing a human. Standard.

## Ranveer's Year of Everything

Ranveer, meanwhile, is operating at a level that borders on absurd. **Dhurandhar** and **Dhurandhar 2** combined for over ₹1,300 crore worldwide, firmly repositioning him as the most bankable male star in Hindi cinema right now. He's now deep in prep for **Pralay**, a ₹300 crore zombie thriller that he's producing under his own banner, **Maa Kasam Films** — a name that tells you everything about the man's energy.

There was, briefly, the **Don 3** exit controversy. The Federation of Western India Cine Employees issued a non-cooperative directive after Ranveer reportedly walked away from the **Farhan Akhtar**-directed sequel. The directive was lifted last week, with both sides encouraged to "engage in constructive dialogue." Translation: everyone calmed down, nobody's suing, and Ranveer is too busy building a zombie apocalypse to care.

## The Privacy Question Nobody Wants to Ask

Not everyone was charmed by the balcony photos. **Hauterrfly** published a pointed piece asking whether recording a pregnant woman from a neighbouring building constitutes journalism or voyeurism. The article noted that **Alia Bhatt** had previously called out similar intrusions — cameras zooming into her living room, photos of her home circulating without consent.

It's a fair question, and one the Indian entertainment press has never been great at answering. DeepVeer didn't pose. They didn't wave. They were inspecting their house, pointing at walls, maybe picking out curtains. The fact that this became content says more about us than them.

## What DeepVeer Means to the Diaspora

For NRIs scattered across the Bay Area and Brampton and Wembley, DeepVeer isn't just a celebrity couple — they're the version of Indian marriage that looks like something you'd actually want. The big rom-com wedding in Italy. The daughter named Dua. The fact that Ranveer shows up to every event looking at Deepika like she invented colour. They're aspirational without being unreachable, glamorous without being cold.

And now they're moving into a ₹119 crore sea-facing palace with a second baby on the way, both of them at the absolute peak of their careers. Bollywood makes love stories for a living, but it rarely produces one this good off-screen.

The balcony photos will keep circulating. They shouldn't have been taken. But if you're going to have your privacy invaded, at least the lighting was beautiful.
